claims.statement: The active workspace has one declared Cargo dependency layer for every workspace package.
claims.falsifier: cargo metadata shows an unassigned package, an upward dependency, a forbidden edge, or a member-local dependency version.

claims.statement: The raw-frame library detects payload tampering and reports incomplete journal tails rather than silently repairing them.
claims.falsifier: a mutated payload passes validation or a torn final record is accepted as a clean journal.

claims.statement: Python experiment records are content-addressable and reject missing pre-registration fields or naive timestamps.
claims.falsifier: the same canonical record receives different hashes, or an invalid record is accepted.

claims.statement: The shared Rust cost model can be called from a JSON-lines research interface without embedding tariff defaults.
claims.falsifier: a missing effective schedule returns zero charges or the app computes fees outside cost-model.

claims.statement: The repository includes a deterministic research-to-paper toolkit, but no strategy is claimed profitable or validated for live trading.
claims.falsifier: A report or README asserts positive alpha/live profitability without licensed point-in-time data, full executable costs, untouched OOS evidence, independent replication and approved controls.

claims.statement: Canonical Upstox/FYERS normalizers preserve vendor timestamp and payload semantics and never infer aggressor side from LTP-only observations.
claims.falsifier: Any normalizer fabricates an exchange sequence, raw packet, confirmed print or aggressor side not supplied by the source.

claims.statement: Point-in-time dataset publication preserves bitemporal listing, corporate-action, universe-membership, event and source-frame lineage and verifies internal artifact integrity.
claims.falsifier: A later-known listing/action is visible to an earlier event, raw prices are mutated, lineage hash sets do not recompute, or an incomplete publication is accepted.

claims.statement: Paper/research OMS and signed permit verifier do not enable live order routing.
claims.falsifier: A feature flag, test signature or verifier result can cause this repository to submit a live broker order without separately approved/certified routing.

claims.statement: The durable OMS commits order intent, an audit event and its outbox command atomically; it never automatically retries a command after dispatch may have begun.
claims.falsifier: The intent can exist without its outbox command after a process crash, an expired DISPATCHING command is automatically resent, or duplicate broker execution IDs are accepted.

claims.statement: Runtime risk evidence is signed only after a root-trusted, fresh, role-scoped set of eight independent signed observations is verified and their source sequences are consumed by a replay ledger.
claims.falsifier: Caller-supplied RiskFacts can be signed through a public API, a tampered/stale/untrusted observation is accepted, or a consumed source sequence can be replayed.

claims.statement: A PIT dataset may be published with a detached Ed25519 signature over a domain-separated canonical manifest digest; verification requires a separately trusted public key and recomputes the artifact and lineage hashes.
claims.falsifier: A signed dataset verifies after manifest/artifact tampering, an unknown signing key is accepted, or source authenticity/completeness is claimed solely from a manifest signature.

claims.statement: The multi-instrument simulator accepts one selected provider stream, models long-only cash reservations across symbols, and never aggregates visible liquidity across provider observations.
claims.falsifier: A mixed-provider replay silently adds displayed depth, an open buy reserve is ignored for another symbol, or a short sale is accepted without inventory.

claims.statement: Release dependency integrity is machine-checked: workflow actions are pinned to commit SHAs, every declared Python dependency is pinned in a resolved constraint set, undocumented advisories fail the audit gate, and the SBOM is generated deterministically from Cargo.lock and the constraint sets.
claims.falsifier: An unpinned `uses:` reference, a declared dependency absent from its constraint file, or an advisory absent from the allowlist passes the gates, or two identical SBOM runs differ.

claims.statement: The versioned exchange reference parsers account for every physical row of a dated source file under a declared version, preserve that outcome on a repeat parse, and fail closed on an undeclared version; compatibility is limited to the tested source versions and categories.
claims.falsifier: A dated source file has a row with no accepted/excluded/rejected outcome, a repeat parse differs from the first, an undeclared format version parses successfully, or a passing run is presented as coverage of untested versions or products.

claims.statement: The shared ingress port preserves original provider bytes and capture metadata for both Upstox raw protobuf frames and FYERS SDK-decoded callback observations, refuses foreign-source or malformed frames, accounts for duplicates and sequence gaps, and replays captured source bytes deterministically into a rebuilt consumer checkpoint after restart without inventing canonical identities.
claims.falsifier: An ingested frame changes its payload bytes or metadata, a foreign-source frame is committed, a duplicate produces a second journal record, a gap or malformed frame is silently ignored, a restart loses the last committed position or payload hash, or an unknown instrument is assigned a canonical identity in the ingress stage.

claims.statement: The fundamental-data validation path rejects malformed company identities and financial facts, validates source-document SHA-256 syntax and evidence locations, validates append-only revisions and derived-fact dependency lineage, and selects only revisions whose publication, observation, ingestion, and required predecessor/input records are known at the requested point in time.
claims.falsifier: A malformed fact or identity is accepted; an invalid document digest or evidence locator passes; a duplicate, broken or cyclic revision/dependency chain passes; a future or unknown-publication fact is selected in a historical as-of view; or the CLI accepts an overlong, aggregate-byte-over-limit, blank, CRLF, BOM-prefixed or torn JSONL record.

claims.statement: A completed FYERS SDK session is imported only after its manifest and full hash chain verify; every record is validated, event and gap metadata survive canonical re-encoding, and repeated imports add no records to the shared raw journal.
claims.falsifier: An invalid manifest or broken chain is imported, a verified record is dropped, gap metadata is lost, or a repeated import adds a second set of journal records.

claims.statement: Canonical projection from Upstox and FYERS verified sources is bound to one exact reference revision and normalizer version, keeps unknown instruments unresolved, requires source-frame hashes, and replays byte-identically in a fresh process.
claims.falsifier: A projection accepts a drifted instrument map, infers an identity for an unknown instrument, omits a source-frame hash when bound, or produces different bytes on a fresh-process replay.

claims.statement: The paper engine consumes a canonical projection only with explicit provider selection, resolved instruments and source-frame lineage; optional reference binding must match the projection, and fresh-process replay is byte-identical.
claims.falsifier: A replay accepts unresolved instruments, unlinked events, a mismatched provider or reference binding, or produces different bytes in a fresh process.

claims.statement: The active SBE decoder reproduces the independent C++ SBE decoder canonical dump for the frozen golden capture byte for byte, re-encodes each message to its exact original bytes, and fails closed on seven malformed inputs.
claims.falsifier: A golden message decodes to a different canonical line, a canonical re-encoding differs from the original bytes, or any of the seven malformed inputs is accepted.

claims.statement: KDB-X analytics is a checked-in, gated repository capability: a typed q contract drives one book per source, its output is pinned by byte-identical golden files and schema-validated digest reports, and a reference check verifies the golden numerically when q is not installed.
claims.falsifier: A q run merges or sums two sources, emits an unknown, missing or duplicated metric, produces different bytes on a fresh process, produces a report that fails its schema, or a golden file that the Rust reference cannot reproduce.

claims.statement: q / kdb+ analytics has the same style-gate treatment as other languages: a canonical style guide with authoritative sources, an added-lines q checker with self-tests wired into make check and CI, and in-process q unit tests over a CSV assertion harness that fail closed on a broken case.
claims.falsifier: A bare / line, unparenthesised count comparison or dotted column access inside a lambda passes the q gate; removing the q checker or its wiring does not fail the style-gate integrity check; or a deliberately failing q assertion exits zero.

claims.statement: Source data rights are tri-state with evidence provenance; UNKNOWN or PROHIBITED never authorizes store or replay, no right is silently upgraded to PERMITTED, and the registry and schema enforce coherent snapshot semantics.
claims.falsifier: An UNKNOWN store/replay right satisfies a requirement, a boolean permission is still accepted, a right changes to PERMITTED without written evidence, or a snapshot_only product declares snapshot=false.
